why: Sort, then compare neighbours: after sorting, the closest pair of values is always adjacent, so one pass over neighbouring differences finds the minimum gap and every pair that achieves it, already in ascending order.
hints: Checking every pair is O(n^2). After sorting, can the closest pair ever be two elements that are not next to each other?
No: if a < b < c then c - a > b - a. So only adjacent pairs of the sorted array are candidates.
Sort, compute the minimum of a[i+1] - a[i], then collect every [a[i], a[i+1]] with that difference. The output is sorted for free. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Each pair is written smaller first, and the list is in ascending order: both come free from the sorted array.
Values are distinct, so the minimum difference is at least 1.
Use two passes (find min, then collect) or reset the list whenever a smaller gap appears.
